target.title: fix(ai): defer simple stream API key validation to async IIFE
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where streaming model functions (e.g. `streamSimpleAnthropic`, `streamSimpleGoogle`, `streamSimpleMistral`, etc.) throw synchronous errors when a provider's API key is missing. Because downstream components expect these functions to always return a stream object and yield errors asynchronously, synchronous throws can cause the system to crash or fail before the stream is returned.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced direct synchronous throws in `packages/ai/src/providers/` (Anthropic, Google, Mistral, OpenAI Responses) with returning an initialized `AssistantMessageEventStream` that asynchronously emits an error event (via `process.nextTick`) and ends.

## User Impact

Prevents application/gateway crashes when keys are missing. Users/clients now receive clean error events in the UI indicating the missing key instead of experiencing unhandled runtime errors.

## Evidence

Passed 51 tests for Anthropic provider, including:
`✓ returns stream immediately and emits error event asynchronously when apiKey is missing`

Execution output:
```
✓ |unit| packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts (51 tests) 88ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  51 passed (51)
```

### Real Behavior Proof

Checked by calling `streamSimpleGoogle` or `streamSimpleAnthropic` without an API key, verifying that it returns a stream object synchronously and yields an async error:
```json
Received asynchronous event: {
  type: 'error',
  reason: 'error',
  error: {
    role: 'assistant',
    content: [],
    api: 'google-generative-ai',
    provider: 'google-generative-ai',
    model: 'google/gemini-1.5-flash',
    stopReason: 'error',
    errorMessage: 'No API key for provider: google-generative-ai'
  }
}
```
